item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03320","case1_error":"Omits Ted’s four eaten cookies, reporting the intermediate remainder of 138 instead of 134.","case2_error":"Correctly finds 10 cakes remaining, then reports 50 already baked as the number still needed.","reason":"Case 1 omits a consumption event; case 2 answers the complementary quantity after correctly computing the requested remainder.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03321","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 120/2 as 60/2 = 30, then gives an unsupported final answer of 15.","case2_error":"Replaces Friday’s 40% increase with a 15% increase applied across five days.","reason":"Case 1 miscalculates a correctly written average; case 2 constructs an incorrect percentage relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03322","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written calorie sum as 2175 instead of 1975.","case2_error":"Divides average weights by group sizes instead of multiplying to obtain total weights.","reason":"Case 1 is numerical evaluation error; case 2 uses incorrect relations between averages, counts, and totals.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03323","case1_error":"Reduces the required rope length by 25% instead of compensating for lost usable rope.","case2_error":"Subtracts money from length; its final expression evaluates to 4000, not the stated 10000.","reason":"Case 1 applies loss compensation backwards. Case 2 mixes quantities and miscalculates its expression; these errors persist despite ambiguity about field dimensions.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03324","case1_error":"Invents an initial count of zero and updates cookie counts inconsistently with removals and returns.","case2_error":"Calculates jewelry spending without deducting the $40 already spent on the sweater.","reason":"Case 1 fabricates the starting quantity and violates inventory arithmetic; case 2 omits a prior expenditure from an otherwise valid budget calculation.","judgment":"different"}]}
